claim_verdicts.evidence: Pinned docs support the per-dependent half: "The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) ...: Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." (options.md:12). No pinned doc states "many small, focused interfaces beat one large one"; grep "segregat" in refs/dotnet-docs finds only this line and a bare list item. The ranking is unconditional and conflicts with the lesson's own section 6 ("a small count is a symptom, not the goal").
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) — no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not use; when different users need different parts of an interface, split it into small, focused interfaces instead of one large one.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." (interfaces.md:86). CS0535 fix: "Provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface, or declare the type as abstract" (interface-implementation-errors.md:140). Lesson text "C# requires a class to provide every member of an interface it implements" drops the default-implementation exception; true for the hypothetical's body-less members.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: On the implementing side, C# requires a class to provide every method the interface declares without a body of its own, which is all four here.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution (SDK 10, net10.0, scratchpad): interface with SendSms and GetDeliveryReport(int, bool); implementer still has GetDeliveryReport(int). Build: "error CS0535: 'Sms' does not implement interface member 'IChannel.GetDeliveryReport(int, bool)'". Doc: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35). Holds for members without a default body, as in the lesson.
git show stage-0:.../INotifier.cs lines 5-8: `public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }` - one member. Code block lines=5-8 matches character-for-character.

git show stage-0: line 5 `public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier`; line 7 private `List<string> sent`; line 9 `IReadOnlyList<string> Sent => sent`; lines 11-16 Send calls Format, sent.Add, Console.WriteLine; line 18 `protected abstract string Format(...)`; lines 21-31 EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier override only Format. Code block lines=21-31 matches.
`git -C examples/don-hang grep -n -i deliver stage-0 -- samples` returns no lines (exit 1). No INotificationChannel or GetDeliveryReport anywhere at stage-0.

"C# doesn't have the concept of checked exceptions. Any method might (in theory) throw any exception." (tips-for-java-developers.md:16) - nothing in the interface signature tells a caller that one implementation throws, so the caller cannot know from the type. The LSP link restates the prerequisite lesson.

Design judgement restating outline misconception 2, not a factual claim about a version. Consistent with the pinned framing of ISP per dependent ("depend only on the configuration settings that they use", options.md:12), which says nothing about member count.
